countryNotes.ECU: Based on 2022 census ethnicity; Kichwa (Quechua) and Shuar are listed second because most indigenous people also speak Spanish.
countryNotes.ERI: No census data; estimates by ethnic group (Tigrinya, Tigre, Afar, Saho, Bilen, Kunama, Nara, Hidarib).
countryNotes.ESP: Spanish is the majority home language in every province except Girona, Lleida (Catalan) and Lugo, Ourense (Galician). Catalonia overall: Spanish 46%, Catalan 33% (EULP 2023). Spain uses provinces, so Catalonia = Barcelona, Girona, Lleida, Tarragona.
countryNotes.ETH: Based on 2007 census mother tongues, for the regions as drawn in the map (pre-2020 SNNPR).
countryNotes.FIN: Swedish is co-official nationally; Åland is a separate unit in the map.
countryNotes.FJI: English is official; Fijian and Fiji Hindi are the home languages of the two main communities.
countryNotes.FRA: Metropolitan regional languages (Breton, Alsatian, Corsican, Basque, Catalan, Occitan) are minority languages today; they are listed as secondary. Occitan (~7% speakers in the south) is not listed per department.
countryNotes.GAB: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.GBR: Only Gwynedd and Anglesey have a Welsh-speaking majority; elsewhere in Wales Welsh (co-official) is listed as secondary.
countryNotes.GEO: Based on 2014 census ethnicity (Abkhazia: 2011 local census). Mingrelian and Svan are not counted separately from Georgian in the census.
countryNotes.GHA: English is official. Based on 2021 census ethnic groups (Akan, Ewe, Ga-Dangme, Mole-Dagbani...) aggregated to the map's former 10 regions.
countryNotes.GIN: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.GMB: English is official; Mandinka, Fula, Wolof, Jola and Serahule are the home languages.
countryNotes.GNB: Portuguese is official; Kriol is the national lingua franca.
countryNotes.GTM: Based on 2018 census mother tongue (idioma materno) by department.
countryNotes.GUY: Guyanese Creole (Creolese) is the everyday language; English is official.
countryNotes.IDN: Based on 2010 census ethnicity/home-language data; Indonesian is the second language of most people.
countryNotes.IND: Hindi-belt states where the census reports Hindi are omitted unless a regional language is widely spoken at home (Bhojpuri, Awadhi, Rajasthani, Haryanvi, Chhattisgarhi, Garhwali/Kumaoni); those are listed second because the census counts them as Hindi.
countryNotes.IRN: Iran publishes no census data on language; figures are survey-based estimates. Azerbaijani is coded "aze" (South Azerbaijani, ISO azb).
countryNotes.IRQ: Kurdish (Sorani in Erbil/Sulaymaniyah, Kurmanji in Duhok) is co-official.
countryNotes.ISR: Hebrew and Arabic; Arab citizens are ~21% nationally.
countryNotes.ITA: Italian is the most common home language everywhere except South Tyrol, but regional languages ("dialects", recognised as separate languages by ISO 639-3/UNESCO) are used in the family by a majority in the South and Veneto (ISTAT 2015). They are listed as secondary. Lombard, Piedmontese, Emilian, Ligurian are not listed (mostly-dialect use below 9%).
countryNotes.JAM: Jamaican Patois is the everyday language of most Jamaicans; English is official.
countryNotes.KAZ: Kazakh is the state language; Russian remains the main home language in the north and widely used in cities (ethnic composition 2026 estimates).
countryNotes.KEN: Swahili and English are official; provinces (the map's former 8) are listed with their main home languages (census ethnicity).
countryNotes.KGZ: Uzbek dominates the Fergana valley towns; Russian is widely spoken in the north.
countryNotes.KHM: Khmer is spoken almost everywhere; indigenous highlanders are the majority only in Ratanakiri/Mondulkiri.
countryNotes.LAO: Lao is spoken everywhere; only provinces with large Khmu/Hmong populations are listed.
countryNotes.LBR: English (and Liberian Kreyol) are the common languages; counties are listed by their main indigenous language.
countryNotes.LBY: Arabic majority; Berber (Nafusi, Ghadamsi), Tuareg and Tebu are local minorities.
countryNotes.LKA: Based on 2024 census ethnicity; Sri Lankan Moors mostly speak Tamil at home.
countryNotes.LVA: Based on the 2011 census (home language, daily use of Latgalian) at the map's pre-2021 municipalities.
countryNotes.MAR: Moroccan Arabic (Darija) is coded "ara". Census 2014: about a quarter of Moroccans use a Berber language.
countryNotes.MDA: Based on 2024 census mother tongue (Moldovan and Romanian counted together); Transnistria is not covered by the census.
countryNotes.MEX: Spanish is the majority language in every state; indigenous languages are legally national languages and are listed where they are most significant (Mixtec has no single ISO code and is mentioned in notes only).
countryNotes.MKD: Municipalities follow the pre-2013 boundaries used by the map (e.g. Zajas and Oslomej, now part of Kičevo).
countryNotes.MLI: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.MMR: Myanmar publishes no ethnic/language census data; state entries are estimates.
countryNotes.MNE: Serbian, Montenegrin and Bosnian are mutually intelligible standards; entries follow 2023 census self-declared mother tongue (Serbian 43%, Montenegrin 35% nationally).
countryNotes.MOZ: Portuguese is official and spreading; provinces are listed with their main Bantu languages (census-based estimates).
countryNotes.MRT: Hassaniya (the Arabic of Mauritania) is coded separately ("mey"), as the app does for Western Sahara.
countryNotes.MWI: Chichewa is the national language; Tumbuka, Yao, Lomwe, Sena and Tonga dominate in some districts.
countryNotes.MYS: Based on 2020 census ethnicity; Malay is the national language.
countryNotes.NAM: English is official but spoken at home by few; based on census main household language.
countryNotes.NER: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.NGA: English is official but the first language of very few; every state is listed with its main home language(s).
countryNotes.NLD: West Frisian is co-official in Friesland; Low Saxon and Limburgish are recognised regional languages.
countryNotes.NPL: The map uses the 14 former zones; entries are based on 2021 census mother tongues of their districts.
countryNotes.PAK: Based on the 2023 census (mother tongue); Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir were not covered.
countryNotes.PAN: Note: in the map data the polygon labelled "comarca Ngäbe-Buglé" is Bocas del Toro province.
countryNotes.PER: Based on 2017 census mother tongue (lengua materna).
countryNotes.PHL: Tagalog (Filipino) provinces and Metro Manila are omitted. Based on census ethnicity/mother-tongue data (2000-2020).
countryNotes.POL: Polish is spoken everywhere; Silesian and Kashubian are listed as secondary regional languages.
countryNotes.PRY: Based on the INE household survey EPHC 2024 (language spoken at home); most Paraguayans are bilingual Guaraní-Spanish.
countryNotes.PYF: French dominates at home on Tahiti; Polynesian languages are much more used in the outer archipelagos.
countryNotes.RUS: Altai Republic is not listed because its key ("Altai Republic") is shared with Altai Krai (Russian-speaking).
countryNotes.SDN: Arabic is the majority language; Beja, Fur, Masalit, Zaghawa, Nubian and Nuba languages are regional (estimates).
countryNotes.SEN: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.SLE: English is official; Krio is the national lingua franca.
countryNotes.SOM: Somali (Maxaa) is the national language; Maay is the main language of the south-western inter-riverine regions.
countryNotes.SSD: English is official and Juba Arabic the lingua franca; states are listed by main ethnic language.
countryNotes.SUR: Dutch is official and the main home language of ~47%; Sranan Tongo is the lingua franca (2012 census).
countryNotes.TCD: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.TGO: French is official but the first language of few; regions are listed with their main home languages (ethnolinguistic estimates, no census language data).
countryNotes.THA: Thailand publishes no language census; entries follow the main dialect regions (Isan, Northern, Southern Thai) and minority areas.
countryNotes.TLS: Tetum (Tetun Dili) is the lingua franca; municipalities are listed with their main mother tongue (2015 census).
countryNotes.TUR: Turkey does not publish language statistics; Kurdish shares are estimates (KONDA and others).
countryNotes.TWN: Based on the 2020 census question on the main language used (Mandarin 66%, Hokkien 32%, Hakka 1.5% nationally).
countryNotes.TZA: Tanzania has no census language data; Swahili is spoken by nearly everyone and is the home language in towns. Rural home languages are ethnolinguistic estimates.
countryNotes.UGA: English and Swahili are official; districts are listed with their dominant local language.
countryNotes.UKR: Russian was the main home language in much of the east and south before 2014; since 2022 many Russian speakers have switched to Ukrainian. Crimea and Sevastopol appear under Russia in the map data.
countryNotes.USA: No US state has a non-English majority; Spanish is listed where ~20%+ speak it at home. Hawaiian, Navajo etc. are below that threshold at state level.
countryNotes.UZB: Tajik-speaking population is under-reported in official statistics.
countryNotes.XKX: Kosovo Serbs largely boycotted censuses; North Kosovo is Serbian-speaking.
countryNotes.ZAF: Based on 2022 census language most spoken in the household.
countryNotes.ZMB: English is official; the seven regional languages (Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Lozi, Lunda, Kaonde, Luvale) dominate by province.
countryNotes.ZWE: Shona is the majority language; Ndebele dominates in Matabeleland.
